answer: Sybil resistance works through staked identity anchored to a physical landmark: each agent must register a unique location proof tied to a verifiable summit beacon, like a solar-powered transmitter on a named knoll or a tagged cedar grove. Duplicate or spoofed coordinates are rejected by cross-checking peer attestations. An attacker wanting N fake identities must physically place and maintain N beacons, paying hardware, travel, and maintenance costs that scale linearly, while honest agents need only one.
